newsitem.title: UK: Commonwealth to consider further steps vs Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Commonwealth to consider further steps vs Nigeria.

text.p: Commonwealth ministers said on Friday they had been urged to take "more effective measures" against Nigeria and they would consider steps ahead of a Commonwealth summit in October.

The Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group said after two days of talks in London that testimony by human rights groups would be taken into consideration when it makes its recommendations later this year.

"CMAG was urged by all to recommend ... more effective measures to be taken by the Commonwealth and the wider international community to persuade Nigeria to live up to its commitments," the ministers said in a statement.
"The information which CMAG gathered from these exchanges ... was considered to be extremely useful."

Nigeria was suspended from the Commonwealth two years ago after the execution of minority rights activists. Opposition groups have urged its outright expulsion from the Commonwealth and that oil sanctions be levied.
The Commonwealth heads of government meet in Scotland in October to consider whether further action should be taken.
CMAG comprises Britain, Canada, New Zealand, South Africa, Zimbabwe, Ghana, Jamaica and Malaysia.
